/feature-flow-lite:feature-flow-lite Modals and popovers built with React Aria don't hide the rest of the page from screen readers when the app is rendered inside a web component's shadow root. `ariaHideOutside` in `@react-aria/overlays` (which `useModalOverlay`, `usePopover` and friends use) only walks and observes the light DOM. So content next to the dialog inside a shadow root stays exposed, and content added later inside a shadow root is never hidden.

Make `ariaHideOutside` work with shadow DOM when the repo's shadow DOM support is turned on (`enableShadowDOM()` from `@react-stately/flags`):

- Everything outside the targets is hidden, including siblings inside the targets' shadow roots and inside every shadow root that encloses them. The hosts on the path to a target stay visible.
- Content added after it runs, anywhere in a target's shadow root or a root enclosing it, gets hidden. Live announcers and top-layer elements stay visible, as they do in the light DOM.
- Targets can live in different shadow roots, such as an input in one and its popover in another.
- The function it returns restores everything and stops observing.
- With shadow DOM support off, nothing changes.

Follow the repo's conventions: tests go next to the existing `ariaHideOutside` tests, and the repo's tests, lint (`yarn eslint`) and type check (`yarn check-types`) must pass. Use `yarn jest <path>` to run tests.
